question: What is the primary tool used in tele-nursing to deliver care?

options.D: Manual blood pressure cuffs and stethoscopes

explanation: Tele-nursing relies fundamentally on electronic communication tools like phones and computers to reach patients remotely. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h1)

question: Why is tele-nursing particularly helpful for patients living in remote areas?

options.A: It brings healthcare services directly to homes without requiring travel
options.B: It guarantees that patients will never need hospital admission
options.C: It provides free medications delivered straight to the doorstep
options.D: It completely replaces the need for any physical doctor visits

explanation: By using technology, nurses can assess and monitor clients who live far away from physical health facilities. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h1)

question: Which device is best suited for automatically sending daily blood glucose readings to a nurse?
explanation: Remote monitoring tools are designed to track and transmit vital health metrics directly to healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h2)

question: How do electronic health records support tele-nursing practice?

options.A: By automatically generating prescriptions without a doctor
options.B: By providing distant nurses with quick access to past patient history
options.C: By allowing patients to perform their own laboratory blood tests
options.D: By replacing the need for any direct verbal communication

explanation: Digital records ensure that nurses caring for patients from afar can easily review previous medical notes and treatments. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of a tele-triage nursing service?

options.A: Conducting mandatory annual physical fitness exams for workers
options.B: Performing emergency major surgeries over a video conference
options.C: Evaluating sudden symptoms and advising on the appropriate level of care
options.D: Dispensing free prescription drugs directly to callers via mail

explanation: Tele-triage involves assessing a caller's symptoms over the phone to guide them on where and how fast to seek medical attention. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h3)

question: A nurse uses a video call to inspect a healing surgical wound for an elderly patient at home. Which model of care does this represent?
explanation: Using video visits to monitor recovery and wound healing at home falls under the home care tele-nursing model. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h3)

question: Which licensing requirement must a tele-nurse always meet when caring for remote clients?

options.A: Holding a valid license in the location where the patient is physically located
options.B: Having a license from any country as long as the nurse has a smartphone
options.C: Possessing a special international internet communication permit
options.D: Registering only with the hospital administration board

explanation: Regulatory bodies require nurses to be legally licensed in the specific jurisdiction where the patient receives the care. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h4)

question: Why is verifying a patient's identity critical during a tele-nursing consultation?

options.A: To ensure the patient is using an approved brand of mobile phone
options.B: To prevent unauthorized persons from receiving confidential health information
options.C: To confirm that the patient has paid their hospital utility bills
options.D: To make sure the patient's internet connection speed is fast enough

explanation: Identity verification protects patient privacy and ensures sensitive medical details are not disclosed to the wrong party. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h4)

question: Which of the following is a common challenge for tele-nursing practice in developing regions?

options.A: Erratic electricity supply and poor internet connectivity
options.B: Patients refusing to use phones for any medical reason
options.C: An overabundance of advanced video monitoring equipment
options.D: Excessive physical contact between nurses and clients

explanation: Unreliable power and weak network signals frequently interrupt remote healthcare delivery in resource-constrained settings. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h5)

question: What is a major clinical advantage of tele-nursing for healthcare systems?

options.A: It lowers the cost of medical equipment to zero
options.B: It guarantees that nurses never experience professional burnout
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any laboratory testing
options.D: It reduces overcrowding in physical hospital wards and clinics

explanation: By managing stable patients remotely, hospitals can ease the burden on physical facilities and focus resources where needed most. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h5)
